event.summary: Update-survival promise omits the explicitly accepted old-terminal migration
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 78e9d68a95119db8452ee139efde13d38546f648. TLDR: Someone trusting the general statement that sessions keep running across an update could leave work in an old terminal that this one migration ends. Precise references: SPEC_impl.md:7777-7784 restores the general update-survival statement; SPEC_impl.md:2784-2834 describes ending the old tmux server, interrupting live old sessions and sweeping their processes; SPEC.md:3001-3016 explicitly specifies that migration. Contract analysis: this is a deliberate specification exception rather than an unintended migration. Exact acceptance text, SPEC.md:3004-3006: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' The reviewed commit message expressly says it is 'accepting that the installer prints it during that one update too.' Suggested bucket: potentially highest because an inaccurate update assurance could contribute to losing running work; could-be-highest: yes. Established consequence is the documented one-time termination; a user actually relying on the restored assurance has not been observed. event.summary: One-shot wake deadline deliberately excludes a later connection wait
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 533169cf19571d34af3a8497eaceb8d2d7b7c852. TLDR: A resumed launch could still hold New and host changes unavailable if it first sees the woken connection, remains waiting for checkout preview past the timer, then sees a connection-pending phase. Source checks: create_form.rs:6284-6297 arms one counter only after successful Resume; 7499-7522 sleeps once and checks the current parked state only at expiry; 1143-1165 treats the old token or a live connection-pending observation as a connection wait; 7534-7556 first validates the parked draft, then returns before inspecting preview failure while that wait is active. 4314-4331 and 4552-4579 show the preview request has its own result, but 7556 precedes the handling of that result. Source basis establishes the single-check limitation, not an observed indefinite execution. The exact source route through a late connecting phase with unchanged incarnation was not established or exercised; a third incarnation instead cancels the parked press through guard_if_current at 1170-1205. Contract disposition: do not report as a bug because the assigned implementation contract explicitly selects this boundary, despite the broader shorthand in SPEC.md:1346-1350. Exact acceptance, SPEC_impl.md:211-214: 'The limit is checked when its 60 seconds run out: a press still waiting for a connection then is discarded, even one that saw the host connect and lost it again before that point, while a host that shows a connection pending again only after that point is not bounded by it.' Suggested bucket if unintended: high/material UX; could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work route identified. Confidence: confirmed one-shot source behavior and exact specification acceptance; the hypothetical late-wait route is not claimed as executed. proposed_drop: the exact quoted specification deliberately excludes a wait that reappears after that checkpoint. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted. This revision resolves lead f2 as a considered candidate, preserving its original suspected consequence. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: Ordinary late disconnect cancels the parked launch; one-shot timer boundary is explicit
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 533169cf19571d34af3a8497eaceb8d2d7b7c852. TLDR of original concern, preserved: a resumed launch might keep New and host changes unavailable if it sees its woken host, waits past the single timeout, then reenters a connection-pending phase. Synthesis resolves the previously missing readily checkable premise against that ordinary disconnect route. Source: manager.rs:5123-5228 publishes client and status coherently; specifically 5190-5203 gives a fresh incarnation whenever the client changes, including when it goes away. connect_phase at 3948-3971 publishes Connecting with no client. Thus a connection lost after the form actually observed the returned connection has a third token, not that observed connection's token. shared.rs:706 projects host.incarnation into HostOption.connection; create_form.rs:989-1005 copies it into PreviewAuthority.incarnation; guard_if_current at 1170-1205 tolerates only the old pre-resume token or the captured returned token. The pending-submit effect at 7534-7547 calls that guard before the awaiting-woken-connection return at 7551-7556, so this ordinary third-token route discards the parked press rather than stranding it. The one-shot implementation remains real: 6284-6297 arms one counter after Resume; 7499-7522 checks the parked state only once at expiry. Exact specification boundary, SPEC_impl.md:211-214: 'The limit is checked when its 60 seconds run out: a press still waiting for a connection then is discarded, even one that saw the host connect and lost it again before that point, while a host that shows a connection pending again only after that point is not bounded by it.' This boundary is explicit despite the broader shorthand at SPEC.md:1346-1350; it does not establish that shipped ordinary disconnects can retain an unchanged token. Suggested bucket if the original route existed unintentionally: high/material UX; could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work route identified. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the normal lost-connection premise and exact contractual timer boundary; no indefinite execution observed. proposed_drop: ordinary late disconnect mints a third incarnation and cancels through guard_if_current; independently, the exact quoted specification excludes a later reappearing wait from the timer's guarantee. No other unchanged-token late-wait producer has been established, and no uninvestigated producer is claimed. possible_cover: none; no queue/ledger/plan coverage sources consulted. Revision preserves original impact while resolving the missing incarnation premise. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed. This can strand an existing running session from the product's ordinary controls, but the restriction is intentional. Source basis: assigned SPEC_impl.md patch removes the supervisor-outside launch, account, hooks and terminal mechanisms and replaces them with a decode-and-delete compatibility path. At the pinned revision, SPEC_impl.md:8646-8656 retains decoding, legacy removal, confirmed absence and creation/deletion lock handling, and permits removal of confinement/attach helpers only 'once nothing can create or open these sessions.' Exact product acceptance, SPEC.md, Retired containerized sessions: 'Existing sessions support Delete only. Opening terminals or tabs, exec, Stop, Restart, Clone, Replace and Replace with are refused.' Exact cleanup requirement: 'Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence.' The replacement ordinary container model is specified separately, with an in-container supervisor; it does not silently reinterpret the old configuration as a new launch. Suggested bucket if unintended: high/material loss of access to running sessions. Could-be-highest: no established unconfirmed destructive route; an explicit Delete is still warned and requires confirmed removal, and this documentation-only patch does not itself stop a running process. Confidence: confirmed explicit compatibility restriction in both specifications; implementation effects not executed. proposed_drop: the exact quoted specification deliberately makes these old experimental sessions delete-only. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted.
